428: The Values, Assemblages and Registry Zenodo zips (10.5281/zenodo.23735569 / 23735996 / 23735970) were downloaded to data/orchid-v2026.10/ (SHA-256 manifests verified; everything except the README is gitignored), and aiida_txdiagram/orchid_compare.py compares them with the stage 07 output of every run (out/orchid_compare/REPORT.md, assemblage_points.tsv, invariants.tsv). Two comparisons are made. (1) Phase regions: the ORCHID interior points (T, x, phase set) that fall inside the run's T grid and composition range are compared with the stable phases read from the two-phase pairs at the nearest grid temperature, giving the prevalence-weighted phase recall S = Σ n_p R_p / Σ n_p of [Arroyave2026]'s §4.2 and the number of exact matches. (2) Invariant reactions: identified by the multiset of phases contained in the two-phase pairs that change across a bracket of 07_invariants.tsv (a same-phase pair p+p counts twice, so the Ag–Cu eutectic is fcc+fcc+liquid); only three-phase reactions and congruent melting are compared with the median of the ORCHID experimental values (extraction_accepted) that carry the same multiset. Entries and exits of same-phase segments (fit noise) and the change where the liquid first touches a solid are not compared. Phase names differ per TDB (FCC_A1/A1_FCC, B2_BCC/BCC_A2, L12_FCC/ALNI3_L12/FCC_4SL, raw labels such as γ′), so they are normalised with a mapping table inside the script.

447: Comparison of the ORCHID-based CALPHAD routes with the MLIP phase diagrams (2026-11-04)
448: ORCHID is not a method for computing free energies, so there are only two ways to "draw a CALPHAD phase diagram from ORCHID". Route 1: draw as they are the phase boundaries and invariant reactions that ORCHID-Diagrams (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23735859, downloaded in addition) stores for each TDB of the SGTE binary collection ([Hallstedt2025], CC BY 4.0), computed with pycalphad 0.11.2 (the TDB files themselves are not included). Route 2: assess the ORCHID ESPEI datasets (10.5281/zenodo.23735788, also downloaded) with ESPEI 0.9.1 (added to env/pycalphad) to build a TDB. Code and results are in ftphase/examples/orchid_calphad/ (README, sgte_diagrams.py, espei_alli/).
449: Route 1 (out/sgte_<sys>.png, out/overlay_<sys>.png): Al–Li 7, Al–Ni 12, Ag–Cu 6 assessments. The invariant reactions differ by only a few K between assessments (Al–Li eutectic 873–876 K, B32 congruent 975 K, Al₂Li₃ peritectic 793 K; Al–Ni L1₂+fcc+L 1643 K, B2+L1₂+L 1642 K, Ni₂Al₃ 1401 K, NiAl₃ 1124 K, B2 congruent 1953 K; Ag–Cu eutectic 1053 K). Fig. 8 overlays the boundaries of the reference assessments (AlLi-20Lon, AlNi-01Dup-4sl, AgCu-04Wit-LB) on the T–x diagrams of all MLIPs/EAMs. This is sufficient as the CALPHAD-side reference for judging the quality of the MLIP phase diagrams.

451: Route 2 (Al–Li, espei_alli/): the Al–Li data in ORCHID consist only of 4 experimental invariant-reaction ZPF records (all eutectic, 1926–1981), 9 phase-region points from hand-drawn diagrams, derived brackets and liquid stability points, DFT formation enthalpies of Al₂Li₃ and Al₄Li₉, and the literature experimental formation enthalpy of AlLi (B32), −20.7 kJ/mol-atom; there are no mixing enthalpies of the liquid or fcc, no activities, no heat capacities and no composition of the Li-side peritectic. 469: Route 2 determines only the Al side. The eutectic temperature and composition land on experiment, but the liquid L0 of −16 kJ/mol was determined from the 4 eutectic points alone (the SGTE assessments are of order −48 kJ/mol). ORCHID has no two-phase data that pin down the B32 congruent melting and the Al₂Li₃ peritectic, and ESPEI's ZPF likelihood only measures whether the specified phases lie on the common tangent and does not penalise intruding phases, so the Li side is left undetermined. A continuation with the ZPF weight raised 5-fold (alli-mcmc2.tdb) matches the eutectic 873 K but makes the liquid and fcc parameters unphysical.
470: Which to use. Route 1 (assessments made by hand from all the data) is the reference for the MLIP phase diagrams. Route 2 is a test of how far ORCHID's machine-extracted data alone can determine things; the next candidate use is to refine an MLIP-derived TDB (the stage 05 output) given as the starting point, as PhaseForge+ does.
